div.head: Ine 74.2
div.ab: Ne þearf se frige mid þam þeowan mæg gieldan, buton he him wille fæhðe ófaceapian, ne se þeowa mid þy frigean.
..þearf se fr:::: ::d .., ..n he him w:::: fæhþe ...
Ne þearf se frigea mid þam þeowan mæg gyldon, buton he him wille fæhðe ofaceapian, ne se þeowa mid þam frigean.
Ne ðearf se frigéa mid ðam ðeowan men gyldan, buton he him sylle fæhðe ofaceapian, ne se ðeowa mid ðam frigean.
Non cogitur liber cum seruo cognationem soluere, nisi uelit eum factione liberare, nec seruus cum libero.
Ne þearf se frige mid þam þeowan mæg gieldan, buton he him wille fæhðe ófaceapian, ne se þeowa mid þy frigean.
Ne þearf se frige mid þam þeowan mæg gieldon, buton he him wille fæhðe ofaceapian, ne se þeowa mid þy frigean.
Der Freie braucht nicht dem Unfreien bei[stehend] Sippezahlung zu leisten — es sei denn, er wolle [freiwillig die] diesem [drohende] Rache abkaufen — noch der Unfreie bei dem Freien.
The free man need not pay kin-payment [standing] with the unfree man — unless he wishes [voluntarily] to buy off the vengeance [threatening] him — nor the unfree man with the free.
A freeman need not associate himself with a relative who is a slave, unless he wishes to ransom him from a vendetta; nor need a slave associate himself with a relative who is a freeman.
The freeman need not pay money for his kinsman along with a slave, unless he wishes to redeem him from a vendetta; nor the slave along with the freeman.
A free man need not pay kin-compensation for a [penal] slave, unless he wishes to protect him from violent retribution, nor need the slave do so for a freeman.

note.label: same usage (mæg)
note.quote: the only other example that Liebermann adduces is Alfred §44.4 [...] hæbbe his mæg forworht

note.label: same term (mægbot)
note.quote: The compound mægbot occurs in i Cnut in respect to violating church peace, for which the offender has to pay his own wer (§2.4)

note.label: parallel usage
note.quote: As discussed in n. 198 to Ine §76, we accept Liebermann's hypothesis that this phrase includes a shift in meaning for mæg

div.note: mid am eowan mæg gieldan. Liebermann suggests that mæg here means “payment for kindred” (cf. wer for wergild), or that we have a compound verb mæg-gieldan. But possibly mæg is an error for the dative mæge, when we could read: “a freeman need not pay along with a servile kinsman”.

Vgl. Gl unfrei 9 d; Sippe 13 e. — Solch Kompositum wie mæggieldan aus subst. + verb., das alle Hss. hier meinen und mein Wb ansetzt, ist auch dædbetan; als Ein Wort schreibt meggildare auch Hn 70, 5. Es ist aber sonst nicht belegt; ich habe es daher im Text in zwei Wörtern gedruckt. ‘Mit unfreiem Menschen zahlen’ B, offenbar unverstanden. Unglücklich ändern mæge Schmid, Toller: dann fehlt das, was oder in welcher Beziehung gezahlt wird. Auch Af 42, 4 heisst mæg ‘rechtliche Folge aus Verwandtschaft’, dort Empfangsanspruch, hier Zahlungspflicht daraus. Gieldan (s. Wb) kann ‘zahlen’ bed., sowohl im Sinne von ‘büssen für Erschlagenen’ als von ‘auslösen des Schuldigen’. Phillpott (Kindred 210) möchte mæggield gieldan emendieren (wofür keine Hs. spricht) und an eine Übersetzung aus Kymrischem denken (von der Ine keine Spur verrät)

Cf. Gl unfrei 9 d; Sippe 13 e. — Like mæggieldan (which all the MSS mean here and my Wb enters), dædbetan too is a compound of substantive + verb; Hn 70, 5 likewise writes meggildare as one word. It is, however, not attested elsewhere; I have therefore printed it as two words in the text. ‘Pay with an unfree person’ B, evidently not understood. Schmid and Toller unhappily alter to mæge: then what is paid, or in what respect, is missing. In Af 42, 4 too mæg means ‘legal consequence arising from kinship’, there a claim to receive, here an obligation to pay arising from it. Gieldan (see Wb) can mean ‘pay’, both in the sense of ‘make compensation for a slain man’ and of ‘ransom the guilty man’. Phillpott (Kindred 210) would emend to mæggield gieldan (for which no MS speaks) and think of a translation from Welsh (of which Ine betrays no trace)
‘he give [money] [in order] to buy off vengeance’ B
‘wolle’, im Ggs. zu ‘muss’ der Rechtssphäre am Satzbeginn: Anruf des Anstandsgefühls der Sippe für den bedauerten Unfreien
‘be willing’, in contrast to the ‘must’ of the legal sphere at the beginning of the sentence: an appeal to the kindred’s sense of decency on behalf of the pitied unfree man

‘ihn von der Feindschaft loskaufen’ (Schmid nach Q) widerspricht der Grammatik des Originals. Falsch ‘from himself’ (Price): nicht dem freien Verwandten, sondern dem unfreien Missetäter droht Rache, da ja die rechtliche Haftung der Sippe fürs Mitglied mit dessen Verknechtung endet

‘buy him off from the feud’ (Schmid, following Q) contradicts the grammar of the original. ‘from himself’ (Price) is wrong: it is not the free kinsman but the unfree wrongdoer who is threatened by vengeance, since the legal liability of the kindred for its member ends, after all, with his enslavement

Thorpe translates ‘unless he be desirous to buy off from himself,’ etc. Schmid, ‘ausser wenn er ihn von der Feindschaft los kaufen will.’ In the MSS mæg gieldan is written as one word, and in Henr. cap. 70 § 5, where this clause is translated, mæggieldan is rendered by megildare. Such compounds are unusual, though not unknown; Liebermann, iii. p. 81, cites dædbetan. It is perhaps better to read thus than to trans. mæg as ‘Sippenzahlung’ (with Liebermann) or to take it as nom.
For frige read frigea (with H, B, and Ld).
